chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us; he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us; he said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Hadhrami, from his father, from Uthman ibn Zayd, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said:

The advent of the Qa'im from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, is like the advent of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and the one from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, who rises before the advent of the Qa'im, is like a young bird that flew and fell from its nest, and children played with it.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt (The People of the House), referring to the Prophet's family and Imams
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Mahdi in Shia eschatology
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Qa'im's emergence and the fate of those who rise before him according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) elevates the status of the Mahdi’s emergence by equating it with the prophetic mission of the Messenger of Allah, underscoring its divine authority and centrality in Shia eschatology. He warns against premature uprisings by the Ahl al-Bayt, likening such early risers to a fledgling bird that falls from its nest, becoming vulnerable to being 'played with' or defeated by enemies, a metaphor for the loss of strategic advantage and potential humiliation. This hadith, found in al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, reinforces the doctrine of *al-Nuzur* (waiting for the signs) and the importance of timing in the Mahdi’s movement.
